HRF_CLIM.claim: Hot summers around 40 °C, cool winters near 6 °C; monsoon rain July–September, more rain December–February.

evidence.quote: Haryana is hot in summer with maximum temperatures hovering around 40 °C (104 °F) and cool in winter with minimum temperatures around 6 °C (43 °F).

Around 29% of rainfall is received during the months from July to September as a result of the monsoon, and the remaining rainfall is received during the period from December to February as a result of the western disturbance.

Reflecting the significance of dairy products in their cuisine, the people of Haryana hold curd and lassi in high regard, incorporating them into various meals, infusing a delightful creaminess into their culinary offerings.

overview.text:
Ladakh is a high-altitude desert often called 'Little Tibet'. It opened to tourism only in 1974, when 527 visitors came; today tourism is its biggest earner.

Leh is the base, with its palace and the great monasteries of the Indus valley — Thiksey, Hemis and Alchi. Over Khardung La lies the Nubra Valley with its dunes and Bactrian camels; to the east are the high lakes of Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri, and to the west Kargil and Dras.

images.alt: A quiet tree-lined street of colonial houses in Pondicherry's White Town
images.caption: White Town, Puducherry

overview.text:
Puducherry — Pondicherry until 2006 — was the capital of French India. It joined India in practice in 1954 and formally in 1963, but its French heritage is everywhere: in the White Town's colonial houses and street names, its bakeries and cafes, and its Franco-Tamil food. It is a small territory: in 2024 it recorded 2.12 million domestic and about 18,000 foreign tourist visits.

The town sits on the coast about 170 km south of Chennai. Its seafront Promenade Beach fills with strollers every evening. The Sri Aurobindo Ashram, founded in 1926 by Sri Aurobindo and the Mother, draws visitors from around the world, and Auroville, the experimental township they inspired, lies about 10 km to the north around its golden Matrimandir.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Puducherry's small airport is at Lawspet; most visitors fly into Chennai, Tiruchirappalli or Coimbatore.

By rail: trains run to Chennai, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata and other major cities.

By road: the East Coast Road from Chennai runs via Mahabalipuram, with daily buses — including air-conditioned ones — from Chennai.
